title: In three fly connectomes, PFN-to-hDeltaB wiring repeats the travel-vector geometry (opposite same-side PFNd/PFNv vectors, 61-62% axonal PFNd input); the left-right angle depends on the PB phase frame
abstract: Question: Lyu et al. (2022) derived from one connectome (hemibrain v1.1) that four PFN populations give hDeltaB neurons four vectors at about +-45 and +-135 degrees, whose sum is the travel direction of the fly. Do other animals have the same wiring? Data: hemibrain v1.2, male CNS v1.0 (both FIB-SEM) and FlyWire v783 (TEM); 40 PFNd, 20-21 PFNv and 18-19 hDeltaB neurons per map; no new downloads. Method: PB phases of PFNs from EPG input (label-free) or from glomerulus labels (four frames); a complex rank-1 fit of the PFN-to-hDeltaB matrix gives the angle and gain of each population; hDeltaB compartments from synapse coordinates (male CNS) or a phase rule (validated 100% in the male CNS); hDeltaB and Poisson resampling; phase-permutation nulls; the Lyu phasor model. Results: if PFNd input on the dendritic arbor is ignored, one phase shift per population explains 91-99% of the matrix in all maps (null 59-62%, p = 0.001). Same-side PFNd and PFNv vectors are 162-179 degrees apart in all maps (one exception: FlyWire, net model, EPG-Delta7 route). PFNd input is 61.7% axonal in the male CNS (coordinates), 61.3% in hemibrain and 60.9% in FlyWire (phase rule), against 61.3% in hemibrain v1.1; PFNv input is 99.9% dendritic. The left-right separation is 71/75/64 degrees (hemibrain/male CNS/FlyWire) in the EPG frame, 88/92/78 with the EPG-Delta7 route and 101/103 with the Delta7 label index: the wiring alone fixes it only to about 30 degrees. A left-right asymmetry of -9 to -20 degrees and a 3-4 fold forward-backward gain imbalance repeat in all maps. PFNa, PFNm and PFNp have similar left-right offsets (79-96 degrees, EPG frame); PFNd is lowest, and FlyWire PFNd is 17-26 degrees lower than in the FIB-SEM maps. Thinning PB synapses to FlyWire density does not reproduce this. The phasor model with each map's vectors errs 1.4-10.8 degrees RMS with pure amplitude modulation but 13-47 degrees with non-negative amplitudes, so PFNv signals must be compensated. Limitations: one animal per map; no activity data analysed; synapse counts as weights; the PB phase frame and synapse efficacy are not known; exploratory method choices.

display.caption: Each hDeltaB neuron receives the four PFN populations (PFNd and PFNv, left and right PB) at four fixed angle offsets in all three connectomes (axon model, EPG-input PB phases). Points: one hDeltaB and one population; lines: fitted vector angles; dotted: +-45 and +-135 degrees.

Rotation-free angle relations with 95% intervals for three maps, four PB phase frames and two efficacy models. Same-side PFNd and PFNv vectors are near 180 degrees apart in all maps; the left-right separation D depends on the PB phase frame (64-104 degrees).

Male CNS synapse coordinates repeat the hemibrain compartment rule: PFNd input to hDeltaB is about 62% axonal and PFNv input is dendritic. A phase rule, validated in the male CNS, gives 61% in hemibrain v1.2 and FlyWire.
